convoLines.text: "So what's your plan here? Just... get through it? Trust me. Mostly."
"Yeah — Honest. I can work with honest."
"Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's butchery. A plan's just a direction you argue with. It'll be fun, probably."
"Still on your plan here."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Funny how that works."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Francisco was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Gerald grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Gerald is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Francisco's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"I was a dockworker — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you did for fun."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I wasn't a paramedic. I was a dockworker. Someone I love needed the lie more than I needed the truth."
Javier looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to protect the group. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Javier rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"That again?" Javier sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I wasn't a pharmacist. I was an ESL teacher. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
The air goes tight. Their eyes narrow, just slightly.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Still on that wound care."
"We went over this," Adaeze says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"About that question — Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone? I mean it."
"What's this about? I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Still on needing to be alone. That means something."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? It'll pass."
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Francisco is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Gerald is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Anyway — I should get going."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on your first memory."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Francisco died... I keep expecting to see Francisco at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Francisco said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Francisco. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Gerald nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on your read on people here. Seen worse."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Extended Warranty? I'm pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Anyway." A small smile.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer. Thank you. Really."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what scares you most."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about Extended Warranty last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Stare' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Gerald shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sure — what's on your mind? What's the worst that happens."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Javier nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Javier digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1054 kcal to the pantry.)
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
They nod. "Okay."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Francisco Duffy is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Francisco is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.
d41: 🕯️ Francisco Duffy is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Francisco kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Francisco's gone." Gerald looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Francisco." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Reagan blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Francisco Duffy, 41 days. The mantle passes to Reagan Tian.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Reagan Tian, 36 — an ESL teacher. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location, War Cry, Dowsing.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Francisco — and Francisco is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Gerald, Javier, Lin and 3 more speak for Reagan — "Francisco trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Reagan before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d71: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
d71: Gerald shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
d71: Javier nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
d71: 🤝 Gerald is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
d71: "I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Javier digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1054 kcal to the pantry.)
